- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, particularly after sharp upward spikes in the history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent highs and underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in the first 5–10 days of the forecast.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the last 5–10 days of history, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Overestimation is more pronounced in the first 10–15 forecast days, then gradually corrects — suggesting a “warm-up” bias.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward trends, especially when history shows a clear decline in the last 5–10 days.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the short-term (1–3 days ahead) and overly pessimistic in the medium-term (5–10 days ahead).
